Fit the two-parameter correction, a + b * lp

Source: R/recalibrate.R
mm_recal_slope.Rd

b below 1 says the predictions are too spread out as well as too high. Clustered the same way as mm_recal_intercept(), and b is the parameter that needs it, because whether b differs from 1 is the question that decides between this form and the constant alone.

Usage

mm_recal_slope(lp, y, cluster = NULL, positive = NULL)

Arguments

lp

Linear predictors from the FROZEN model, not refitted here. For an mm_model() these are fitted(model, scale = "link") on new rows.

y

The observed outcome, in any form mm_model() accepts.

cluster

An identifier for rows that are not independent, or NULL.

positive

The level that means the event, as in mm_project().

Value

A list: a, b, se_a, se_b, b_z, b_p, n, events, cluster_robust, n_clusters, and a one-line reason.

Details

The test on b is against 1, not against 0. A slope correction of 1 is no correction, so the null that matters is b = 1; testing b = 0 would ask whether the model discriminates at all, which is a different question and one mm_validate() already answers.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 400, seed = 9)
fit <- suppressWarnings(mm_model(
  mm_project("recal", "event", c("age", "bmi"),
             positive_class = 1, cohort = cohort), cohort))
lp <- as.numeric(fit$fit$linear.predictors)
mm_recal_slope(lp, cohort$event, positive = 1)$b
#> [1] 1
